audit_items.details: The Authorization type referenced (fork_types/SG-004) pertains to EIP-7702 set-code authorizations, which are specification-level constructs. Prysm is a consensus layer client; EIP-7702 authorization validation occurs in the execution layer (EL) client, not in Prysm (CL). Component mismatch: EL vs CL.

The Authorization.nonce field referenced (fork_types/SG-004) pertains to EIP-7702 set-code authorizations. This is an execution layer (EL) concern. Prysm is a consensus layer client and does not validate EIP-7702 authorization nonces. Component mismatch: EL vs CL.

The extract_deposit_data function (requests/SG-001) is specification pseudocode from the consensus specs. In Prysm's Go implementation, deposit processing uses different structures and methods. No direct 1:1 mapping of this specification function exists in the codebase. The actual implementation uses Go-native deposit handling with SSZ decoding.

The extract_deposit_data offset validation (requests/SG-001) is specification pseudocode. Prysm implements deposit data extraction using SSZ (Simple Serialize) library functions rather than manual offset checking. The specification's offset constants (pubkey_offset, withdrawal_credentials_offset, etc.) are implicit in SSZ schema definitions.

The extract_deposit_data size validation (requests/SG-001) is specification pseudocode. In Prysm, deposit data field sizes are enforced through SSZ type definitions and automated SSZ validation, not through explicit size checks in application code.

The extract_deposit_data output concatenation (requests/SG-001:q_concat) is specification pseudocode describing the deposit data structure layout. Prysm uses SSZ-defined DepositData structs where the 192-byte layout is enforced by type definitions, not by explicit concatenation logic.

The validation failure paths in extract_deposit_data (requests/SG-001) are specification pseudocode. In Prysm, deposit validation failures are handled through Go error returns and SSZ unmarshaling errors, not through 'InvalidBlock' exceptions as described in the specification pseudocode.

The parse_deposit_requests function (requests/SG-002:q_check_addr) is specification pseudocode for validating deposit contract address in execution layer logs. In Prysm, deposit ingestion from the execution layer uses Engine API and the deposit contract address validation is handled at the execution layer boundary, not in application-level pseudocode.

The parse_deposit_requests topic validation (requests/SG-002:q_check_topic) is specification pseudocode. In Prysm, deposit event signature validation occurs during Engine API processing and log parsing using the execution payload's deposit data, not through explicit topic hash comparisons in application code.

The parse_deposit_requests ordering requirement (requests/SG-002:q_iter_keys,q_iter_logs) is specification pseudocode describing canonical deposit ordering. In Prysm, deposits are received in canonical order from the execution layer via Engine API, and ordering is implicitly enforced by the execution client, not by explicit iteration logic in consensus layer code.
